The _.unset and _.omit functions in Lodash are vulnerable to prototype pollution. The fix for CVE-2025-13465 only guards against string key members, so an attacker can bypass the check by passing array-wrapped path segments. This allows deletion of properties from built-in prototypes such as Object.prototype, Number.prototype, and String.prototype. The issue permits deletion of prototype properties but does not allow overwriting their original behavior. The issue is patched from 4.18.0 to 4.18.1 depending on the package: lodash, lodash-es, and lodash-amd in 4.18.1, and the standalone lodash.unset and lodash.omit packages in 4.18.0.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in INTINITUM FORM Transliterator serbian-transliteration allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects Transliterator: from n/a through 2.5.13.

A high privileged remote attacker can exploit an unauthenticated SQL Injection vulnerability in the getVpnData function due to improper neutralization of special elements in a SQL SELECT command. This can result in a total loss of confidentiality.
Rejected reason: This CVE ID has been rejected or withdrawn by its CVE Numbering Authority, replacedby CVE-2026-70640.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, there is a stack-based out-of-bounds write / stack-buffer-overflow in bacnet-stack when the server processes a malicious Atomic-Read-File request in record access mode. The bug is triggered on the real server side. A crafted request can set an excessively large RecordCount, which is later used as the loop bound for writing record data into a stack-allocated BACNET_ATOMIC_READ_FILE_DATA data structure. However, the stack object only has space for one fileData element. When the loop reaches i = 1, the code computes &data->fileData[1], which is already out of bounds, and the resulting invalid pointer is passed down to memmove(), causing a stack-buffer-overflow. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.0 to before 1.4.4, and 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, a NULL pointer dereference can be triggered in bacnet_device_object_reference_decode() when a WriteProperty request updates OBJECT_STRUCTURED_VIEW / PROP_SUBORDINATE_LIST. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1, a remote attacker can trigger an uncontrolled recursion and stack overflow in the default server application of bacnet-stack by abusing the Channel object. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4 and 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a RemoveListElement request targeting Notification-Class.recipient-list can trigger a stack-based out-of-bounds write in the current master branch when the request contains more than NC_MAX_RECIPIENTS valid BACnetDestination elements. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a stack-buffer-overflow can be triggered in the current master branch when a Loop object reads a referenced property through its default timer path and the referenced property is OBJECT_STRUCTURED_VIEW / PROP_DESCRIPTION containing a long attacker-controlled string. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.4, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, there is a remotely reachable denial-of-service vulnerability in bacnet-stack affecting the default demo server built from the unmodified apps/server/main.c. This issue has been patched in version 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.2 to before 1.4.5, and 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, a signed fileStartPosition taken from AtomicReadFile and AtomicWriteFile stream-access requests is not validated tightly enough before it reaches the RAM file backends. Practical impact includes: reliable denial of service via process crash, out-of-bounds read that may expose adjacent memory contents, or out-of-bounds write that may corrupt heap memory and destabilize the process. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5 and 1.5.1.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2, a reachable out-of-bounds write exists when encoding the device.address-binding property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0-rc2.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, the bsc_node_parse_urls() function in src/bacnet/datalink/bsc/bsc-node.c contains three distinct bugs when parsing space-separated WebSocket URIs from a BACnet/SC Address Resolution ACK message. Two bugs cause out-of-bounds writes past the utf8_urls[10][129] array in the static BSC_ADDRESS_RESOLUTION structure. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a Denial of Service (DoS) vulnerability exists in the BACnet stack's ReadPropertyMultiple (RPM) handler. When processing a malformed RPM request packet that lacks the expected closing tags, the function handler_read_property_multiple enters an infinite loop. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, there is a library-level memory safety issue that is reachable from an unmodified official sample server (apps/server-basic/main.c) over BACnet/IP resulting in a stack-use-after-return in writable Device string properties. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

IBM Bob 2.0.3 allows unauthorized extensions to retrieve session tokens via the authentication provider API. The token is exposed in the account identifier field during account enumeration, without requiring explicit user consent. This may allow malicious extensions to access sensitive session information and potentially perform unauthorized actions on behalf of the user.

In multiple locations, there is a possible use-after-free due to a logic error in the code. This could lead to remote code execution with no additional execution privileges needed. User interaction is not needed for exploitation.

In _vqueue_get_avail_buf_locked of trusty/kernel/lib/trusty/vqueue.c, there is a possible Double-read / TOCTOU due to a race condition. This could lead to local escalation of privilege with execution privileges needed. User interaction is for exploitation.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a BACnet/SC peer can trigger a heap out-of-bounds read (up to 3 bytes), pre-authentication, in the BACnet/SC header-option decoder. bvlc_sc_decode_proprietary_option() reads the vendor-id and option-type at fixed offsets [3],[4],[5] before checking the option's declared header length, and the option-list validator never enforces a minimum length for proprietary options. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, there is a remote global-buffer-overflow in the official router-ipv6 application shipped with bacnet-stack, this results in an out-of-bounds write to the global transmit buffer under ASan. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

Edito CMS deserializes JSON data without further validation. A user (even an administrator) cannot exploit this vulnerability through the application's normal functionality. An attacker who could modify cache entries or inject them could execute code on the server.




This issue was fixed in version 5.10.2607.  Hotfixes for older versions (5.8) have also been released.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in BuddyBoss Buddyboss Platform buddyboss-platform allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects Buddyboss Platform: from n/a through 3.0.5.

A high privileged remote attacker can perform a code injection in the backends backup restore function leading to code execution. This can result in a total loss of confidentiality, integrity and availability.
The backups created by the application use a weak static password allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to access their content. This can result in a total loss of confidentiality.

The Android implementation of the Flutter/Dart receive_sharing_intent package, versions 1.4.1 through 1.9.0, contains a path traversal vulnerability in FileDirectory.getDataColumn that allows a malicious co-resident application to write files outside the intended cache directory by supplying a crafted _display_name value from an untrusted ContentProvider. Attackers can use a path-shaped display name ../databases/proof.txt combined with a controlled content stream to write to arbitrary locations within the receiving application's private sandbox under its UID, achieving file overwrite without user interaction.

Dell SmartFabric OS10 Software, versions prior to 10.6.0.10, contains an Incorrect Authorization vulnerability. A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to Command execution.

rabbitmq-c is a C-language AMQP client library for RabbitMQ. Prior to version 0.17.0, a heap buffer overflow exists in rabbitmq-c when the public amqp_send_frame() API is used to serialize an oversized AMQP_FRAME_BODY. The issue occurs because amqp_frame_to_bytes() copies frame.payload.body_fragment.len bytes into the connection outbound buffer without validating that the body fragment fits within the allocated frame buffer. An application that passes an oversized body frame to amqp_send_frame() can trigger a heap out-of-bounds write, resulting in process crash and memory corruption. This issue has been patched in version 0.17.0.

Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an SQL Command ('SQL Injection') vulnerability in StylemixThemes uListing ulisting allows Blind SQL Injection.This issue affects uListing: from n/a through 2.2.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, lighting_command_decode in src/bacnet/lighting.c decodes its first field with the bounded apdu_size - apdu_len, but every nested decode in the operation switch is called with the original full apdu_size while the read pointer has been advanced to &apdu[apdu_len]. The leaf decoders bound their reads against the size they are told, so they read up to apdu_len bytes past the end of the caller's buffer, resulting in an out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a remote out-of-bounds read exists in the official BACnet client application apps/readpropm in bacnet-stack commit e2bdbf6. When readpropm sends a legitimate ReadPropertyMultiple request to a malicious BACnet/IP peer, the peer can reply with a malformed but structurally valid ReadPropertyMultiple-ACK that drives the client into a global-buffer-overflow read on the global receive buffer Rx_Buf. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0, a malformed but non-empty BACnet WriteProperty request can drive the official server demo into a non-terminating request-processing loop with repeated heap-backed side effects. This results in a remote unauthenticated denial of service via uncontrolled resource consumption and a non-terminating request path. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE implementation accepts AtomicWriteFile(record-access) requests that replace existing records with caller-controlled content. If a client replaces a record with shorter data, the backend can shrink the heap allocation and then continue processing with a trailing-copy length derived from the old layout. During that replace path, the RAMFS backend computes the trailing-copy length from the old file layout, then shrinks the heap allocation, and finally uses the stale length in memmove(). As a result, the source range of that memmove() can extend beyond the end of the reallocated heap buffer, producing a heap out-of-bounds read. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the RAMFS-backed FILE object implementation stores appended records as NUL-terminated strings, but its record-counting logic later walks the buffer as if an additional terminating empty record were present. As a result, two consecutive AtomicWriteFile(record-access) append requests can cause record_count() to call bacnet_strnlen() on a pointer that is already one byte past the end of the heap allocation. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to version 1.5.1, the BACnet FILE object implementation allows remote WriteProperty(PROP_FILE_SIZE) requests to change the size of a stream-access FILE object without checking whether that FILE is marked Read_Only. When the FILE backend is RAMFS, enlarging the file only performs realloc() and updates the stored size; the newly exposed tail region is not initialized before later reads. As a result, a remote client can enlarge a read-only RAMFS-backed stream-access FILE and then immediately retrieve the newly exposed region with AtomicReadFile(stream-access). Depending on the allocator and build configuration, the returned data may contain sanitizer fill bytes, stale heap contents, or other unintended process memory. Shrinking the file through the same path can also remotely truncate content that was intended to be read-only. This issue has been patched in versions 1.5.1 and 1.6.0.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability that allows authenticated attackers to access another user's private mail by supplying a crafted reloadMailTypeId parameter to Ctrl::getCurObj() without a readRight() ownership check in CtrlMail.php. Attackers can manipulate the mail identifier value, such as reloadMailTypeId=mail-1, to retrieve the title and body of private messages belonging to other users, resulting in unauthorized disclosure of sensitive communications.

Omnispace Agora Project through 26.10.0 contains a broken access control vulnerability in which the isAutor() function in MdlObject.php grants accessRight=3 based solely on object authorship without verifying the user still belongs to the object's space. Attackers who were previously members and authored objects can retain unauthorized read access to space objects even after being removed from the space, leading to persistent information disclosure.

OpenMRS module bahmnicore contains Core OpenMRS modules for Bahmni (including ERP & ELIS Atom Feed Clients). In version 0.93, an attacker with authenticated access could potentially exfiltrate sensitive data from the database. This issue has been patched in version 0.93.1.

augment-vir is a collection of helper functions. Prior to version 31.73.5, the grep() function exported by @augment-vir/node inserts caller-controlled search patterns directly into a double-quoted shell command string without sanitization (grep.ts:310). When the constructed command is passed to spawn() with shell: 'bash' (shell.ts:98-99), bash evaluates $() command substitution expressions embedded in the pattern, resulting in arbitrary OS command execution as the Node.js process user. Any downstream application that passes untrusted input to grep()'s pattern or patterns field is vulnerable to unauthenticated local (and potentially remote) code execution. This issue has been patched in version 31.73.5.

bird-lg-go is a BIRD looking glass in Go. Prior to version 1.4.7, unsanitized input path enables arbitrary local file read, allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to read sensitive files such as /etc/shadow and /root/.bash_history. This issue has been patched in version 1.4.7.

Group-Office is an enterprise customer relationship management and groupware tool. Prior to version 26.0.37, go/modules/community/bookmarks/controller/Bookmark.php's description() action takes a fully attacker-controlled url parameter and passes it, unvalidated, to \GO\Base\Util\HttpClient::request(). HttpClient::_initRequest() sets CURLOPT_URL directly from this value with no host/IP validation at all. This can result in SSRF via Bookmark/description JMAP action. This issue has been patched in version 26.0.37.

pam_usb provides hardware authentication for Linux using removable media. From version 0.8.0 to before version 0.9.3, the deny_remote feature in pam_usb uses /usr/bin/w -i to detect whether the authenticating user has an active remote tmux session. In pusb_tmux_has_remote_clients() (src/tmux.c), the IPv6 detection regex required exactly four explicit colon-separated groups of 1-4 hex digits (e.g. 2001:0db8:85a3:0000). Any IPv6 address in compressed notation — including loopback (::1), link-local (fe80::1), and global unicast addresses (2001:db8::1) — did not match this pattern. As a result the remote-client check silently returned "no remote clients" even when a remote tmux client was connected from such an address. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.3.

Waline is a comment system with backend support. In versions 3.15.2 and prior, the @waline/client UserList widget builds its DOM by concatenating server-returned commenter fields directly into root.innerHTML with no HTML escaping. The commenter nick and link are stored and returned verbatim by the server (only the comment body is sanitized), and the link field is never sent to the spam filter. So an unauthenticated visitor who posts a comment with link = x"> achieves stored cross-site scripting that executes, with no interaction, in the browser of every visitor to a page that embeds the UserList widget. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.5 and 1.5.1, a single unauthenticated BACnet/IP UDP datagram (port 47808) triggers an out-of-bounds read in xy_color_decode() (src/bacnet/lighting.c), reachable pre-authentication through two default-registered service handlers: the UnconfirmedRequest WriteGroup service (0x0A) and Confirmed WriteProperty on a BACnetXYColor-typed property. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.5, 1.5.1, and 1.6.0.

OpenSearch Dashboards is an open-source data visualization tool designed to work with OpenSearch. From versions 2.14.0 to before 2.19.6, and 3.0.0 to before 3.7.0, a Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in OpenSearch Dashboards exists in the fetchDataSourceMetaData route. The sibling test_connection route validates incoming endpoint URLs via isValidURL() against configured endpointDeniedIPs and endpointAllowlistedSuffixes lists, but fetchDataSourceMetaData accepts the same input shape without performing this validation. An authenticated user can supply an internal or loopback endpoint to probe internal network resources. This issue has been patched in versions 2.19.6 and 3.7.0.

sync-rpc runs asynchronous commands synchronously by putting them in a separate proces. Prior to version 1.3.7, if an attacker could guess the correct port and it was not blocked via a firewall, it was possible to load and execute arbitrary JavaScript files stored on the server running sync-rpc. This issue has been patched in version 1.3.7.

ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.4, several project mutation endpoints under /api/projects/[id]/* resolve the caller's project role but never enforce it, so a user who was granted only the read-only viewer role on a project can perform write operations on that project. The most severe is POST /api/projects/[id]/graph, which deletes every block and link in the project and re-inserts client-supplied ones. A viewer can silently rewrite or wipe the entire canvas of a project they were invited to read. The application clearly intends viewer to be read-only: the collaborators endpoint, the automation endpoints, and the realtime Yjs sync path all reject write attempts from viewers. These specific HTTP handlers simply omit the guard their siblings enforce. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.4.

Livewire PowerGrid creates data tables based on Laravel Livewire library. From version 6.0.0 to before version 6.10.4, the public Livewire property sortDirection is interpolated verbatim into a raw SQL ORDER BY clause and is not restricted to asc/desc, allowing arbitrary SQL injection through POST /livewire/update. This issue has been patched in version 6.10.4.

Hubleys is a dashboard for self-hosted services. Prior to version 0.5.2, any authenticated (non-admin) Hubleys user can upload a file with an arbitrary extension as their dashboard "background image," and the server will later serve that file back with a Content-Type derived straight from the attacker's chosen extension - so uploading an .html file gets it served as text/html. Because the endpoint that serves it returns a manually-constructed response rather than going through SvelteKit's normal page-rendering pipeline, the app's configured Content-Security-Policy never gets attached to it either, so a script embedded in the upload runs unrestricted. This issue has been patched in version 0.5.2.

Heym builds and runs agentic systems and business-process automations on self-hosted infrastructure. Prior to version 0.0.70, heym hardens one untrusted-code path but not its sibling. The Python tool executor (python_tool_executor.py) treats user code as untrusted and mandates a Docker sandbox (no network, read-only fs, non-root, no docker socket), failing closed. The skill executor (skill_python_executor.py) runs skill Python via a local backend subprocess with no Docker isolation — only a 512 MB RLIMIT and a 7-key env denylist — so a skill executes inside the backend execution context, with filesystem access, network egress, and non-denylisted environment variables that should not be exposed to untrusted/shared skills. In the shipped Docker config (backend runs as root + /var/run/docker.sock mounted), this escalates to host root. This issue has been patched in version 0.0.70.

ideon is a self-hosted visual workspace. Prior to version 0.9.5, ideon's link-preview endpoint requires no authentication at all and forwards any URL a caller supplies straight into a server-side fetch. The app does have a general-purpose SSRF guard (safeFetch/validateSafeUrl in src/app/lib/ssrf.ts), but this route sits behind no login check whatsoever, making it a fully open, anonymous URL-fetch relay - and the guard's IP blocklist itself has a gap that lets it reach the server's own loopback interface via the 0.0.0.0 "any address" bypass, a well-documented SSRF-filter evasion technique on Linux. This issue has been patched in version 0.9.5.

bit-vec is a compact vector of bits. Prior to version 0.10.0, there is undefined behavior if a user performs deserialize from an untrusted source and unsafe get_unchecked. A user of this library may be impacted by incorrect behavior if they perform deserialize from an untrusted source and run operations on the deserialized BitVec. This issue has been patched in version 0.10.0.

Paaster is a pastebin application. Prior to version 3.3.0, Paaster's "view once" (burn-after-reading) paste mode can be bypassed with concurrent requests. The check that's supposed to enforce single-use is a plain read followed by a separate write, with no atomicity, so multiple simultaneous requests can all see the paste as "not yet read" and all successfully retrieve it. This issue has been patched in version 3.3.0.

fulgur converts untrusted HTML/CSS into PDF, commonly on a server that processes input supplied by many tenants. From version 0.6.0 to before version 0.33.0, quadratic style-list reprocessing during containing-block resolution for absolutely-positioned pseudo-elements cause denial of service. This issue has been patched in version 0.33.0.

PolicyPress is a compliance policy management tool for small and mid-size teams. Prior to version 1.4.1, sensitive content is disclosed via CSS-only web redaction and insecure starter workflow defaults. This issue has been patched in version 1.4.1.

Budget Board is an app for tracking monthly spending and working towards financial goals. Prior to version 3.6.2, Budget Board's OIDC login flow finds and signs into an existing local account purely by matching the email address asserted in the identity provider's token - it never checks the standard email_verified claim. If the configured OIDC provider ever allows a user to register or display an email address without proving they own it , an attacker can register there using a victim's email and get signed into the victim's existing Budget Board account - including all their linked bank data. This issue has been patched in version 3.6.2.

Hugo Blog is a tech blog site. In commit 744ca15 and prior, the AI assistant proxy exposes three HTTP endpoints (POST /api/blog-assistant, POST /api/blog-search-embedding, POST /api/blog-search-rerank) without any authentication check. When deployed following the documented Nginx reverse-proxy setup, any unauthenticated remote attacker can send arbitrary requests that the proxy forwards to the upstream LLM/embedding/rerank API using the operator's server-side API key (OPENAI_API_KEY / AI_SEARCH_API_KEY). This enables unlimited quota consumption, cost exhaustion, and potential service unavailability for the operator. At time of publication, there are no publicly available patches.

llama.cpp builds b1886 through b7445 contain a race condition use-after-free vulnerability in the LLaMA-Android JNI wrapper where bench_1model() and free_1context() lack synchronization, allowing Thread A to operate on freed memory while Thread B concurrently frees the llama_context. Attackers can exploit this by performing heap spray with attacker-controlled data containing a fake vtable to hijack the vtable pointer at offset +0x30, causing llama_batch_allocr::clear() to dereference arbitrary memory and achieve remote code execution.

A flaw was found in AWX. The debug API endpoints (/api/debug/task_manager/, /api/debug/dependency_manager/, /api/debug/workflow_manager/) are registered unconditionally in the URL configuration and use AllowAny permission class with _ignore_model_permissions=True. This allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to repeatedly invoke scheduler operations that acquire database advisory locks and open transactions, potentially leading to resource exhaustion and degraded service availability.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains a broken access control vulnerability that allows an authenticated Webservice API key holder to read and modify customer records belonging to any shop in a multi-shop installation. Attackers can exploit the missing record-level shop ownership check in shopHasRight() and saveEntityFromXml() to read sensitive customer data such as password hashes and secure keys, and change a customer's email and password via create, update, and delete requests, resulting in account takeover.

PrestaShop before 8.2.9 and 9.2.1 contains an authorization flaw in the Webservice API that allows an attacker holding a key restricted to one shop to act on data of every shop by submitting requests with id_shop=all or id_shop_group=N, which expand the shop context without validating the key's actual shop associations and cause shopHasRight() to evaluate the expanded set as a disjunction. Attackers can exploit this flaw via classes/webservice/WebserviceRequest.php to read, modify, or delete data belonging to shops they are not authorized for, including full customer records such as email addresses, secure_key, and password hashes across the installation.

U-Boot before 2027.01-rc1 contains an out-of-bounds write vulnerability in the video_display_rle8_bitmap function in drivers/video/video_bmp.c. Attackers can supply a crafted RLE8-compressed BMP image to corrupt memory adjacent to the framebuffer and crash the bootloader.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a remote code execution vulnerability that allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to run root commands by advertising a rogue automesh controller over mDNS. Attackers on the upstream Ethernet segment can advertise _cudycmagent._tcp records pointing to a malicious MQTT broker, then send commands encrypted with a fixed AES key that router/batchcmd.lua executes as root.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains an argument injection vulnerability that allows a malicious or compromised ACS to inject curl options through unfiltered Username and Password values in the easycwmpd Upload handler. Attackers can embed whitespace to add options like -o and --url to the root-run curl command, writing attacker-controlled HTTP responses to arbitrary files on the device.

Cudy TR3000 before 2.5.42 contains a command injection vulnerability in luci/model/cbi/vpn/openvpn/client.lua, which embeds the shellquote()-quoted remote host token of an uploaded OpenVPN configuration inside an already single-quoted sed program run by os.execute(), so the nested quotes terminate the outer quote. Authenticated administrators can upload an .ovpn file whose remote host token contains a semicolon to execute arbitrary commands as root.
Zoho Corporation ManageEngine ADAudit Plus versions below 8711 are vulnerable to an authenticated second order SQL injection vulnerability affecting ADAudit Plus custom reports module.

NocoBase is an AI-powered no-code/low-code platform for building business applications and enterprise solutions. Versions 2.1.0 through 2.1.14 contain a server-side request forgery vulnerability in the customRequests:send endpoint. A low-privileged authenticated user can override the stored request URL at runtime using options.url, causing the NocoBase server to send requests to attacker-controlled or internal destinations. Exploitation could expose internal services, Docker host gateways, or cloud metadata endpoints and allow the server to be used as a trusted network proxy. This issue has been fixed in version 2.1.15.
IBM DataStage on Cloud Pak for Data 5.4.0.0 could allow a remote authenticated attacker to obtain sensitive information due to a server-side request forgery vulnerability.
Dell PowerStore contains a content-injection vulnerability. An unauthenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability to display misleading text on the genuine login page for phishing.
Dell PowerStore contains an OS Command Injection vulnerability. A high-privileged attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to arbitrary root command execution on the appliance.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. From versions 1.4.0 to before 1.4.6, 1.5.0 to before 1.5.1, and 1.6.0 to before 1.6.1, the BACnet MS/TP receive path decodes COBS frames into an output pointer inside the same fixed input buffer, but passes the full input-buffer size as the decode capacity. A long valid COBS payload can therefore write past the end of the actual remaining buffer. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.1, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.

VITEC EZ TV Platform Server before 8.5.0 contains an unrestricted file upload vulnerability in the upload handler that allows unauthenticated remote attackers to upload arbitrary files by supplying a target filename in the X-FILENAME request header with no authentication or file type validation required. Attackers can upload a malicious ASPX file directly to the web-accessible uploads directory, where it is immediately executable by the web server, achieving remote code execution in the context of the web server process. Patches are available for versions 8.3.0, 8.3.1, 8.4.0, and 8.4.1. Users running releases prior to 8.3.0 should upgrade to 8.5.0+.

V programming language standard library net.http through version 0.5.2 prior to commit 4077484 contains a TLS certificate validation bypass vulnerability that allows on-path attackers to intercept HTTPS traffic by exploiting the default false value of SSLConnectConfig.validate and FetchConfig.validate, which completes TLS handshakes without verifying certificates in both the mbedtls and OpenSSL backends. Attackers can present an expired, self-signed, wrong-hostname, or untrusted-root certificate to successfully complete the handshake via http.get, http.post, or http.fetch, enabling interception or modification of HTTPS traffic unless validate: true is explicitly configured.

A flaw was found in Foreman’s Api::V2::PersonalAccessTokensController, where Foreman::Controller::UserAware#find_user resolves the target account using User.find(params[:user_id]) without applying the required parent-user authorization check. An attacker with the create_personal_access_tokens permission can therefore invoke POST /api/v2/users/:user_id/personal_access_tokens with another user’s ID and create a Personal Access Token on their behalf. The resulting plaintext token is returned in the API response, while PersonalAccessToken#check_permissions_after_save only validates create_personal_access_tokens on the token and does not enforce edit_users authorization on the target user. The attacker can then use the forged token to authenticate as the victim, potentially resulting in complete account takeover, including administrator accounts.

Dell PowerStore contains an External Control of File Name or Path vulnerability. A remote authenticated attacker could exploit this vulnerability, potentially leading to privilege escalation on the appliance.
Dell PowerStore contains an authorization-bypass vulnerability that could lead to elevation of privilege to administrator.

Dolibarr before 24.0.2 contains an insecure direct object reference vulnerability in the REST Documents API for the ticket module that allows authenticated API users to access ticket attachments belonging to other companies by omitting a company-scope check that is only applied via a session variable set during public ticket authentication, which REST API authentication never sets. Attackers with ticket read permission can enumerate predictable ticket identifiers and supply them to the documents endpoint or download path to retrieve sensitive attachments such as invoices and contracts belonging to other third parties.

Dell Terraform for ObjectScale and Powerstore, versions prior to 1.1.1 (ObjectScale) and versions 1.2.1 through 1.3.0 (PowerStore) contains an insertion of sensitive information into Log File vulnerability in the client initialization component.  A low privileged attacker with remote access could potentially exploit this vulnerability, leading to information exposure and unauthorized access.

HashiCorp Vault and Vault Enterprise are vulnerable to an issue in the integrated storage join process that may allow an unauthenticated attacker with network access to a new, uninitialized node to cause that node to send credentials from its server environment to an attacker-controlled server. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92735) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault's Login MFA feature did not consistently enforce the lifetime of pending two-phase login requests. This may allow a user who previously completed the first authentication factor to complete MFA and obtain a Vault token after the pending request should have expired, including after the user's primary credential has been rotated. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-92738) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.26.

A flaw was found in Ansible Operator Plugins. A low-privileged Kubernetes user can exploit a Jinja2 template injection vulnerability by crafting malicious custom resource (CR) specification values. These values are processed by Ansible without proper sanitization, allowing embedded Jinja2 expressions to be executed within the operator pod. This can lead to arbitrary code execution and privilege escalation, granting the attacker control over the operator's service account with cluster-wide permissions.

Vault's audit devices did not validate the contents of a configured audit log prefix and did not consistently enforce the server-level setting that restricts audit log prefixing. This may allow a privileged operator to inject content into audit logs, potentially leading to forged or misleading audit records. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93333) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

Vault Community Edition and Vault Enterprise did not consistently apply explicit ACL policy deny rules to request paths that differ only by a trailing slash. This may allow an authenticated user who holds a broader delete permission on system configuration paths to disable a secrets engine, auth method, or audit device that a more specific deny rule was intended to protect. This vulnerability (CVE-2026-93335) is fixed in Vault Community Edition 2.2.2 and Vault Enterprise 2.2.2, 1.21.14, and 1.19.25.

IBM ContextForge MCP Gateway 1.0.0 through 1.0.11 is potentially vulnerable to denial of service due to uncontrolled regular expression complexity (CWE-400 / ReDoS). An authenticated user with tool-registration privileges can embed catastrophically backtracking regex patterns in a tool's JSON Schema `pattern` field; when ContextForge validates arguments against that schema, the validation call may consume unbounded CPU, potentially degrading gateway availability.

OS command injection in the TFTP provisioning module of Zenitel EdgeAudioClient before 9.6.3.0, and 10.x before 10.1.3.0, on VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices allows unauthenticated adjacent attackers to execute arbitrary commands as root via a crafted DHCP option 66 (TFTP Server Name) value supplied by a rogue DHCP server on the same network segment. The DHCP-supplied value is passed to a shell without sanitization. Devices using DHCP, the default configuration, are affected on every boot and lease renewal.



The same injection is also reachable via the config_update_tftp_server and sw_update_tftp_server configuration fields by an attacker able to modify the device configuration.

Path traversal in the certificate upload endpoint (/api/certificate/upload) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to write arbitrary files as root via a crafted filename parameter in a multipart upload request when the type field is set to any value other than https_certificate. In that case, both path validation and certificate content validation are skipped.



This can be escalated to arbitrary code execution as root, for example by overwriting startup scripts or planting SSH keys.

Path traversal in the certificate.deleteCertificate JSON-RPC method (POST /api/rpc) of the turbineweb web interface in Zenitel VSFF6, VSFF8, VSFF8MP, VSFF8MN, and VSFT devices with software versions from 10.0.3.0 before 10.1.3.0 allows authenticated administrators to delete arbitrary files as root via a relative path (../) in the file_name parameter.



This can be used to cause denial of service or render the device inoperable by removing critical system files, and to weaken device security by removing files such as firewall rules or certificate trust stores.

The pREST database REST API in Zenitel Connect firmware before 1.11.0 signs and verifies JWTs with the platform CA private key, which is stored on a data volume shared between containers, and sets the PostgreSQL session role from the unvalidated sub claim of each request while connected to the database as the "postgres" superuser, which allows local attackers who can read the platform CA private key from the container filesystem to execute database operations as the PostgreSQL superuser, including reading the master encryption key and password hashes, via a forged JWT with sub=postgres sent to the pREST API.

The host configuration watcher in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 applies a rsyslog configuration file written to a data volume that is shared with the hiatus application container, which allows local attackers with write access to the hiatus container filesystem to execute arbitrary OS commands as root on the host operating system via a crafted rsyslog configuration file.

OS command injection vulnerability in audio messages API in Zenitel Connect before 1.11.0 allows remote authenticated users to execute arbitrary OS commands as root in the hiatus application container via filename parameter to the /api/system/audio_messages endpoint.

Poste Italiane Postecert FIRMAOK! 1.6.29 on Windows contains a local privilege escalation vulnerability caused by an uncontrolled OpenSSL search path, where launcher.exe and dependent executables such as updater.exe and tslupdater.exe load OpenSSL configuration and library files from a hardcoded, user-writable directory that does not exist by default. This makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to extract sensitive company data including owner and member WordPress user IDs, company billing email addresses, credit balances and full credit histories with admin user IDs, per-member purchase limits and spend totals, and shared-cart records containing purchase-order numbers.

BACnet Stack is a BACnet open source protocol stack C library for embedded systems. Prior to versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, and 1.6.1, the BACnet/SC message decoder walks the header-option list by following each option's MORE bit. Nothing rejects a list whose last option still has the MORE bit set, and the decode walk has no upper bound on how many options it processes. A single crafted BVLC-SC frame makes the walk advance one option past the end of the message and read message[message_len], one byte out of bounds. When the bytes after the message carry more MORE-set option markers, the walk keeps going: it runs past the fixed 4-entry option array and writes decoded option fields out of bounds. On the server that decode array is the static global bsc_dm, so the out-of-bounds write lands in adjacent BSS. Both faults are reachable before authentication, from the first frame a peer sends on a BACnet/SC connection, and the bytes that follow the message are the same peer's prior-frame data. This issue has been patched in versions 1.4.6, 1.5.2, 1.6.1, and 1.7.0.
